statements.attributed: hydrogen accumulates in voids and gets trapped at vacancies, dislocations and internal interfaces
statements.quote: Once hydrogen has entered into metals it accumulates in voids and gets trapped at vacancies, dislocations and internal interfaces, i.e. at lattice defects which determine the physical, chemical and mechanical properties of metals.

statements.attributed: excellent mechanical properties under various temperatures
statements.quote: The five-component equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy, also referred to as Cantor’s alloy, is one of the most appealing HEAs due to the high thermodynamic stability of its single face-centred cubic (f.c.c.) structure and the excellent mechanical properties under various temperatures.

statements.attributed: significant decrease in both strength and ductility after hydrogen charging
statements.quote: Figure 2a reveals that the alloy Inconel 718 (56Ni-18Fe-18Cr-5Nb-3Mo), a benchmark material for tolerance against hydrogen embrittlement, shows significant decrease in both strength and ductility after hydrogen charging.

statements.attributed: hydrogen could be controlled to increase the ductility and yet reduce the flow stress
statements.quote: It has also been reported that hydrogen could be controlled to increase the ductility and yet reduce the flow stress of some intermetallic-based titanium alloys.

statements.attributed: a slight decrease in elongation and resistance to gaseous hydrogen embrittlement superior to that of 304 and 316 L austenitic stainless steels
statements.quote: Recent work by Zhao et al. showed that a gaseous hydrogen charged equiatomic HEA with a hydrogen concentration of ~76.5 wt.ppm exhibitts a slight decrease in elongation, although it showed resistance to gaseous hydrogen embrittlement that is superior to that of 304 and 316 L austenitic stainless steels.

statements.attributed: gradient in hydrogen concentration from the edge to the inner regions of the samples could have been induced
statements.quote: Since hydrogenation in the present study was conducted by cathodic charging in alkaline solution and the tensile tests were performed under in-situ hydrogen charging conditions, a gradient in hydrogen concentration from the edge to the inner regions of the samples could have been induced according to previous studies on hydrogen embrittlement of other materials.

statements.attributed: deformation twinning can occur in this HEA at relatively high strain levels at room temperature
statements.quote: A few deformation nanotwins in the CoCrFeMnNi HEA sample without hydrogen were observed (Fig. 4a), which is consistent with a previous study which showed that deformation twining can occur in this HEA at relatively high strain levels at room temperature.

statements.attributed: nanotwinning is revealed by ECCI analysis using bulk samples to avoid any thin slice size and related effects
statements.quote: We reveal the nanotwinning here by ECCI analysis using bulk samples to avoid any thin slice size and related effects which alter the stress and microstructure state of the material.

statements.attributed: relatively low intrinsic stacking fault energy (~19 mJ·m2)
statements.quote: The equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA has a relatively low intrinsic stacking fault energy (~19 mJ·m2), which explains the occurrence of mechanical twinning at room temperature without hydrogen charging.

statements.attributed: hydrogen decreases the stacking fault energy
statements.quote: This is consistent with the previous studies on the effect of hydrogen on the stacking fault energy in other f.c.c. structured alloys, .

statements.attributed: increase in the density of nanotwins leads to an associated increase in work hardening, which postpones the formation of geometric instabilities to higher strain values
statements.quote: These results also show that the increase in the density of nanotwins that we observe in the CoCrFeMnNi HEA leads to an associated increase in work hardening (Supplementary Fig. 3), which postpones the formation of geometric instabilities to higher strain values, thereby increasing strength and ductility simultaneously.

statements.attributed: formation of nanotwins leads to continuous grain fragmentation by the introduction of new interfaces which effectively reduces the dislocation mean free path, hence, causing further strengthening
statements.cited_system: nano-grained copper with embedded nano-twin bundles
statements.quote: The beneficial influence of nanotwins on strain hardening is commonly attributed to the “dynamic Hall-Petch” effect, i.e. the formation of nanotwins leads to continuous grain fragmentation by the introduction of new interfaces which effectively reduces the dislocation mean free path, hence, causing further strengthening, .
